CARBON EMISSIONS.assignment_details:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

GAMING COMPANY.assignment_details:
Problem Statement

A gaming company is developing a simple game where players earn points by completing different missions. Depending on the mission completed, the player's score increases by different amounts. The game also rewards bonus points for high scores and determines the player's current game level.

Develop a Java program using control statements (if-else, else-if, and switch) to manage the game's scoreboard and progression.

Scoring Rules

The player enters:

· Current Score

· Mission Completed

· Number of Coins Collected

The mission number determines the points earned.

Mission | Description | Points Awarded
1 | Defeat Enemy | +50
2 | Rescue Villager | +100
3 | Find Treasure | +150
4 | Defeat Boss | +250
Any other number | Invalid Mission | +0

Bonus Rules

After updating the score:

· If score is 500 or above, award 100 bonus points.

· Otherwise, no bonus is awarded.

Level Rules

Determine the player's level using if-else-if:

Score Range | Level
Less than 200 | Beginner
200–399 | Intermediate
400–699 | Advanced
700 or above | Master

Coin Reward

If the player collected 50 or more coins, display:

Extra Life Awarded!

Otherwise display:

Keep Collecting Coins!

Input

The program receives:

· Current Score

· Mission Number

· Coins Collected

Expected Output

· Updated Score

· Bonus Awarded

· Final Score

· Player Level

· Coin Reward Message

SMART LIBRARY RECOMMENDATION SYSTEM.assignment_details:
Problem Statement

A digital library aims to provide personalised book recommendations to its readers based on their borrowing habits and membership type. Develop a Java program to model this system using two classes: Reader and RecommendationEngine.

The Reader class should store the Reader ID, Reader Name, Number of Books Borrowed, and Membership Type (Gold, Silver, or Regular) as private instance variables with appropriate public getter methods. Use a parameterized constructor to initialize all reader details.

Each membership type is assigned recommendation points as follows:

Membership Type | Recommendation Points
Gold | 30
Silver | 20
Regular | 10

The Recommendation Score for each reader is calculated using the formula:

Recommendation Score = (Number of Books Borrowed × 5) + Membership Points

To determine whether a reader is eligible for a premium recommendation, create a separate class named RecommendationEngine containing the following method:

boolean eligible(Reader r)

A reader qualifies for a premium recommendation if the Recommendation Score is greater than or equal to 80. The Reader class should contain a method named checkEligibility() that internally creates an object of the RecommendationEngine class and invokes the method using:

engine.eligible(this);

This checkEligibility() method should return the eligibility status obtained from the RecommendationEngine.

The program should read the details of multiple readers, store all Reader objects in an array, calculate the recommendation score for each reader, determine their eligibility for premium recommendations, and display the details of every reader along with the recommendation score and eligibility status.

Input Format

ReaderID

Name

BorrowedBooks

MembershipType

Output Format

ReaderID

Reader Name

Recommendation Score

Eligible or Not Eligible

Sample Input and Output

Input | Output
101; Arun Kumar; 12; Gold | Reader ID : 101; Reader Name : Arun Kumar Recommendation Score : 90; Eligible

SMART LOGISTICS ROUTE OPTIMIZER.assignment_details:
Problem Statement

A logistics company wants to analyse the efficiency of its delivery trucks by maintaining details of every truck in its fleet. Each truck record contains the Truck ID, Driver Name, Distance Travelled (in km), and Fuel Consumed (in litres). Develop a Java program that models each truck using a Truck class with private instance variables and public getter methods. The class must demonstrate a parameterized constructor to initialize all truck details.

The program should calculate the mileage of each truck using the formula:

Mileage = Distance Travelled / Fuel Consumed

Based on the calculated mileage, classify the truck's performance according to the following criteria:

Mileage | Performance
Mileage ≥ 18 | Excellent
15 ≤ Mileage < 18 | Good
10 ≤ Mileage < 15 | Average
Mileage < 10 | Poor

The program should store all Truck objects in an array. After processing all the trucks, determine and display the details of a specific truck with the highest mileage, calculate and display the average mileage of all trucks, and display the count of trucks belonging to each performance category (Excellent, Good, Average, and Poor).

Input Format

An integer n, representing the number of trucks.

For each truck:

Truck ID

Driver Name

Distance Travelled

Fuel Consumed

Output Format

Highest Mileage Truck

<Truck ID>

<Driver Name>

< Mileage xx.xx >

<Performance Category>

<Average Mileage xx.xx>

<Number of Excellent Trucks>

<Number of Good Trucks>

<Number of Average Trucks>

<Number of Poor Trucks>

Sample Input and Output

Input | Output

AIRPORT BAGGAGE HANDLING SYSTEM.assignment_details:
Problem Statement

An international airport maintains information about passengers checking in their baggage. Each passenger record contains the Passenger ID, Airline Name and Total Baggage Weight (kg).

Develop a Java program using a Passenger class with private instance variables and a parameterized constructor to initialize all passenger details.

The airport provides a common Free Baggage Allowance (kg) for all passengers. Since this value is common to every passenger, it should be stored as a static variable.

If the total baggage weight exceeds the free baggage allowance, the excess baggage charge is calculated as:

Excess Charge = (Total Baggage Weight − Free Baggage Allowance) × ₹500

Otherwise, the excess charge is ₹0.

In addition to instance methods, implement a static method that updates the free baggage allowance for all passengers.

The program should:

Read the details of 2 passengers.

Set the common free baggage allowance (20 kg) using static block.

Calculate the excess baggage charge for every passenger.

Display the details of both passengers.

Find the passenger paying the highest excess baggage charge and return his/her ID.

Invoke the static method setFreeAllowance() to reset the static variable to 30 kg.

Recalculate the excess baggage charge for every passenger and display their sum.

Input Format

For each of the 2 passengers, read the following details:

Passenger ID

Airline Name

Total Baggage Weight (in kg)

Output Format

For each passenger, display:

Passenger ID

Airline Name

Excess Baggage Charge

And then display:

Passenger ID who is paying the Highest Excess Baggage Charge

Sum of Updated Excess Baggage Charge of both passengers

Sample Input and Output

Input | Output
101; Air India; 35; 102; IndiGo; 25 | 101; Air India; 7500.00; 102; IndiGo; 2500.00; 101; 2500.00

MOVIE STREAMING SUBSCRIPTION ANALYSIS.assignment_details:
A movie streaming company maintains information about its subscribers to analyse subscription revenue and viewing patterns. Each subscriber record consists of the Subscriber ID, Subscription Plan (Basic, Standard, or Premium), Number of Movies Watched, and Monthly Subscription Fee. Monthly subscription fee is assigned based on the subscription plan:

Subscription Plan | Monthly Subscription Fee
Basic | ₹299
Standard | ₹499
Premium | ₹799

The company announces a common Festival Discount Percentage that is applicable to every subscriber, irrespective of the subscription plan. Implement a static method named setDiscountPercentage(double discount) to initialize or modify the common discount percentage before processing the subscriber records. To encourage subscribers to watch more movies, the company also provides an Additional Viewing Discount based on the total number of movies watched by all subscribers.

Number of Movies Watched | Additional Viewing Discount
Less than 10 | 0%
10 to 19 | 2%
20 or more | 3%

The Final Subscription Fee for each subscriber is calculated using the formula:

Final Subscription Fee = Monthly Subscription Fee × [1 − ((Festival Discount Percentage + Additional Viewing Discount) ÷ 100)]

Using an array of Subscriber objects, process all subscriber records and display the required results.

Additional Constraints

The festival discount percentage will be in the range 0 to 20.

The final subscription fee should be displayed with two decimal places.

Collections such as ArrayList should not be used.

Input Format

An integer n, representing the number of subscribers.

A double value representing the common festival discount percentage.

For each subscriber:

Subscriber ID

Subscription Plan (Basic, Standard, or Premium)

Number of Movies Watched

Output Format

· Subscriber ID with Highest Final Subscription Fee (If more than one subscriber has the highest final subscription fee, display the details of the first subscriber encountered)

Number of Basic Subscribers

Number of Standard Subscribers

Number of Premium Subscribers

Number of Subscribers Who benefited from additional discount.

Number of Subscribers Whose Final Subscription Fee is Greater Than or Equal to the Average Final Subscription Fee of all subscribers

POPULARITY OF A USER'S RECENT POSTS.assignment_details:
A social media company wants to analyze the popularity of a user's recent posts. Every day, the platform stores the number of likes received by each post. To understand user engagement, the company calculates the total likes, average likes, identifies the most liked post, and determines whether the user's content is Trending.

As a Java programmer, you are asked to develop a program using a for loop to process the likes received by multiple posts.

This activity demonstrates how companies like Instagram, Twitter (X), and Facebook analyze millions of posts every day to recommend content, improve user engagement, and personalize feeds.

Problem Requirements

Write a Java program that:

1. Accepts the number of posts uploaded by a user.

2. Uses a for loop to read the number of likes for each post.

3. Calculates:

o Total Likes

o Average Likes

o Maximum Likes

4. Determines the engagement level:

o Trending Creator if average likes ≥ 500

o Popular Creator if average likes is between 200 and 499

o Growing Creator otherwise

Input

· Number of posts

· Likes received for each post

Output

· Total Likes

· Average Likes

· Maximum Likes

· Creator Engagement Level
